/s/
suf. 1. (enclitic, morpheme) 의 — A possessive marker, indicating that an object belongs to the noun or noun phrase bearing the marker.

/ˈeɪ̯.ʃən/
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) -화 — An action or process.
suf. 1. (morpheme) 버거 — Used to make the names of hamburgers served in buns with the addition of the specified foodstuff, or with that foodstuff used in place of the usual meat.
suf. 1. (morpheme) -짱 — Appended to a person's name (usually a female, child, a close friend, or an intimate) to add politeness. It is sometimes used to denote cuteness or familiarity.

/d/
suf. 1. (morpheme) -았 — Used to form past tenses of (regular) verbs. In linguistics, it is used for the base form of any past form. See -t for a variant.

/ɪst/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 가장, 제일, 최(最)- — Used to form the superlative of adjectives and adverbs.
suf. 1. (morpheme, not-comparable) -배 — Used to make adjectives meaning "times".
suf. 1. (morpheme) 게이트 — Combined with a relevant place, person, activity, etc. to form the names of scandals.
suf. 1. (morpheme) 각형 — Forms the names of plane figures containing a given number of internal angles, and thus bounded by that number of line segments (polygons).
suf. 1. (morpheme) -면체 — Forms the names of solid figures bounded by a certain number of planes (polyhedra).

/ɪk/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 적 — Used to denote certain chemical compounds in which a specified chemical element has a higher oxidation number than in the equivalent compound whose name ends in the suffix -ous. For example sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) has more oxygen atoms per molecule than sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃).

/ɪ.fɪˈkeɪ.ʃən/
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) -화 — Forms nouns denoting the act or process whereby a subject becomes something else.

/ɪfaɪ/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 화(化)하다 — Forms transitive verbs meaning "to make" from adjectives and nouns.

/-ɪz(ə)m/
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) -주의, -이즘 — Used to form names of ideologies expressing belief in the superiority of a certain class within the concept expressed by the root word, or a pattern of behavior or a social norm that benefits members of the group indicated by the root word. (Based on a late 20th-century narrowing of the "terms for a doctrine" sense.)

/-ɪst/
suf. 1. (morpheme) -주의자, 가 — a person who studies or practices a particular discipline;

/-aɪt/
suf. 1. (derogatory, morpheme, sometimes) 석 — Used to form nouns denoting followers or adherents of a specified person, idea, doctrine, movement, etc.

/-ˈaɪtɪs/
suf. 1. (morpheme, uncountable, usually) -염 — Denoting diseases characterized by inflammation, itself often caused by an infection.

/əti/
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) 성 — Used to form an uncountable noun from an adjective; especially, to form the noun referring to the state, property, or quality of conforming to the adjective's description.

/ɪv/
suf. 1. (morpheme) -적 — An adjective suffix signifying relating or belonging to, of the nature of, tending to, or serving to; as: affirmative, active, conclusive, corrective, diminutive.

/-ˌaɪˈzeɪ.ʃən/
suf. 1. (US, countable, morpheme) -화 — Forms nouns denoting the act, process, or result of doing/making what is denoted by the noun/adjective.

/-ɑjz/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 화(化)하다 — to make what is denoted by the noun/adjective
suf. 1. (morpheme) 군 — Appended to a young man's name or nickname to indicate familiarity.

/lənd/
suf. 1. (morpheme, uncountable) 국 — Used to form the name of a territory, country, or region.

/-lədʒɪst/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 학자 — A person who studies or is an expert in the related -logy.

/-lə.d͡ʒi/
suf. 1. (morpheme, uncountable, usually) 학 — A branch of learning; a study of a particular subject.
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) -음, -기 — Attached to a verb to form a noun meaning the action denoted by the verb or its result.

/-mɪ.tə/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 계 — Used to form the names of measuring devices.

/nəs/
suf. 1. (countable, morpheme, uncountable) ㅁ — Appended to adjectives to form nouns meaning "the state of being (the adjective)", "the quality of being (the adjective)", or "the measure of being (the adjective)".
suf. 1. (morpheme) -피디아 — A general encyclopedia in the structure described by the prefix.

/-ˈfəʊ.bi.ə/
suf. 1. (morpheme, uncountable) 공포증, 포비아, 혐오증 — Used to form nouns meaning fear of a specific thing.

/s/
suf. 1. (morpheme) -들, -네 — Used to form regular plurals of nouns.
suf. 1. (informal, morpheme) 상 — Honorific ending used to indicate that a person is Japanese, talking with a Japanese, or treated like a Japanese.

/tiːn/
suf. 1. (morpheme) 열... — Used to form cardinal numbers from thirteen to nineteen.

/-θ/
suf. 1. (morpheme) -째, 제-, ~ 번째 — Used to form the ordinal numeral when the final term of the spelled number is not “first”, “second”, or “third”.

/-ʃən/
suf. 1. (countable, idiomatic, morpheme) -션 — Used to form nouns meaning "the action of (a verb)" or "the result of (a verb)". Words ending in this suffix are almost always derived from a similar Latin word; a few (e.g. gumption) are not derived from Latin and are unrelated to any verb. More often, -ation is used.

/ti/
suf. 1. (morpheme) ...십 — A nonproductive suffix indicating single-digit integer multiples of ten.

suf. 1. (morpheme) ㅁ직 — Suitable or safe for; capable of enduring or able to bear; able to withstand.
2. (morpheme) ㅁ직 — Able to be; fit to be; -able.
